questions.prompt: State the condition on \(a\) for \(az+b=0\) to have a unique complex solution.
questions.answer: The coefficient must satisfy \(a\ne0\). Then every non-zero complex number has a reciprocal, so \(z=-b/a\) is the unique solution.

questions.prompt: Solve \(2z+6=0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
questions.answer: Subtract \(6\) to get \(2z=-6\). Divide by \(2\), so \(z=-3\).

questions.prompt: Solve \(iz+4=0\).
questions.answer: Move the constant term: \(iz=-4\). Divide by \(i\): \(z=-4/i=4i\), since \(1/i=-i\).

questions.prompt: Solve \((1+i)z=2\) and give the answer in standard form.
questions.answer: Divide by \(1+i\): \(z=2/(1+i)\). Multiply by the conjugate: \(z=2(1-i)/((1+i)(1-i))=2(1-i)/2=1-i\).

questions.prompt: Solve \((2-i)z=5+i\).
Solve \((1+i)z+2\overline{(1-i)}=0\), treating \(z\) as the only unknown.
questions.answer: First simplify the constant: \(\overline{(1-i)}=1+i\), so the equation is \((1+i)z+2(1+i)=0\). Since \(1+i\ne0\), divide by \(1+i\) to get \(z+2=0\), hence \(z=-2\).

questions.prompt: Find \(z\) if \((4+i)z=7-2i\), then verify by substitution.
Classify the solutions of \(0z+(3-i)=0\).
questions.answer: The equation becomes \(3-i=0\), which is false. Therefore there is no complex number \(z\) satisfying the equation.

questions.prompt: Find all complex \(z\) satisfying \((1+i)z+(2-i)=3z\).
questions.answer: Bring \(z\)-terms together: \(((1+i)-3)z=-(2-i)\), so \((-2+i)z=-2+i\). Since the coefficient is non-zero, \(z=(-2+i)/(-2+i)=1\).

questions.prompt: Solve \(\dfrac{z}{1+i}+\dfrac{z}{1-i}=4\).
For which complex numbers \(b\) does \((2-i)z+b=0\) have the solution \(z=1+2i\)?
For which real values of \(t\) does \((t+i)z=1\) have a unique complex solution?
questions.answer: A unique solution exists exactly when the coefficient \(t+i\) is not zero. For real \(t\), \(t+i\) has imaginary part \(1\), so it is never zero; every real \(t\) works.

questions.prompt: Find all real \(t\) for which \((t-2i)z=t^2-4\) has solution \(z=0\).
questions.answer: Substitute \(z=0\): the left side becomes \(0\), so we need \(t^2-4=0\). Hence \(t=2\) or \(t=-2\); both values are allowed because the coefficient is not relevant when checking the given solution.

questions.prompt: A learner solves \((1-i)z=2\) and writes \(z=1+i\). Diagnose the answer by substitution and correct it if necessary.
questions.answer: Substitute: \((1-i)(1+i)=1-i^2=2\), so the learner's value satisfies the equation. The answer is correct: \(z=1+i\).

questions.prompt: Explain why the equation \((a+bi)z+c=0\) can fail to have a unique solution, where \(a,b,c\in\mathbb R\).
questions.answer: The coefficient of \(z\) is \(a+bi\). If \((a,b)\ne(0,0)\), it is non-zero and there is one solution. If \(a=b=0\), the equation is \(c=0\): it has no solution when \(c\ne0\), and every complex \(z\) is a solution when \(c=0\).

questions.prompt: Show that \((1+2i)z+(3-i)=0\) has exactly one solution and find it.
questions.answer: The coefficient \(1+2i\) is non-zero, so a unique solution exists. Isolate: \((1+2i)z=-3+i\), hence \(z=(-3+i)/(1+2i)=((-3+i)(1-2i))/5=(-1+7i)/5\).
